 Meredith College Introduces New Career Promise
 Published 
 Sat, November 14, 2026 
 Meredith College will help cover student loan payments for qualifying graduates, in partnership with Ardeo Education Solutions, and highlight post-graduation career support under the Meredith Career Promise, an initiative the women’s liberal arts college announced today. 
 The Meredith Career Promise bolsters StrongPoints , a strengths-based advising and personal coaching program, as part of the College’s commitment to students’ lifelong professional and financial success. Designed to address the gender-based wage gap in the workforce, the Meredith Career Promise positions Meredith as the only college in North Carolina, and the only women’s college, to offer loan repayment assistance to all incoming students. 
 Loan repayment assistance will be available for qualifying first-year or transfer students who begin their studies at Meredith in fall 2027. Career support is available to all Meredith graduates, both at no extra charge.  
 “These enhancements deepen the impact of StrongPoints to give graduates greater confidence, flexibility and financial security as they launch careers in a competitive and rapidly changing job market,” Meredith President Aimee Sapp said. “As women continue to face barriers, it’s essential to build on our long tradition of preparing them for leadership and rewarding, meaningful work.” 
 Women still earn less than men for comparable jobs, and the pay gap widened from 2023 to 2025 despite women’s educational gains, Forbes reported . Women’s median earnings in the U.S. are 83% of men’s, according to the American Community Survey . 
 Under the Meredith Career Promise, the College will help cover a graduate’s student loans if she works at least 30 hours a week and earns less than $50,000 a year. Participating graduates in the Meredith Loan Repayment Assistance Program will be reimbursed for some or all of qualifying monthly educational loan payments. The program covers federal and private loans, including those secured by parents and legal guardians to cover a student’s education.  
 Meredith is partnering with Ardeo Education Solutions for its loan repayment assistance program. Ardeo is a public benefit company committed to increasing access to the life-changing impact of higher education. As a provider and administrator of Loan Repayment Assistance Programs, Ardeo partners with colleges and universities to reduce the fear of student loan debt and give students and families greater financial confidence in their college investment. 
 More repayment assistance details were announced November 14 at Think Meredith, an open house for prospective students. 
 Meanwhile, career support under the Meredith Career Promise will provide all alumnae access to lifetime services such as one-on-one career exploration, resume and cover-letter reviews, mock interviews, job-search strategies, graduate-school preparation and the college’s online job-opening database known as Handshake.  
 Post-graduation career support has been available to Meredith alumnae, but many alumnae reported not knowing about the services offered. By being more explicit about the offerings, the College hopes more alumnae will take advantage of lifelong career services. 
 “With these steps, we’re telling our graduates that Meredith is still in your corner. We’re showing you a lifelong commitment,” said James McGhee, the vice president for student affairs. “We believe in you, we are invested in your success, and we will continue to walk alongside you wherever your journey takes you.” 
 “Guidance is especially important when careers pivot, go on hiatus, or otherwise enter new phases,” said Courtney Jordan-Steele, the interim director of career services. “That’s why career support shouldn’t end at graduation. The Office of Career Planning’s personalized services help alumnae build confidence, advocate for themselves, tap into our strong alumnae network, and stay current on workforce and hiring trends.” 
 For more information about the Meredith Career Promise, visit meredith.edu/career-promise. 
 Melyssa Allen – Director of Public Relations
